newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy leftists said more open to Stet sale.
newsitem.headline: Italy leftists said more open to Stet sale.

text.p: Italy's hard-left Communist Refoundation party seems to be softening its opposition to the government's planned privatisation of state telecoms holding Stet, posts ministry Undersecretary Vincenzo Vita said.
"Tension seems to be subsiding," Vita told reporters attending a telecommunications conference.
"The government has given guarantees of its seriousness over both the question of a stable shareholding and a golden share," he said.
The government and Refoundation are negotiating the planned sale of Stet later this year which the hard-left ideologically opposes.
Communist Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti said on Thursday that the talks to resolve potentially destabilising differences with the main party in the centre-left coalition had been useful.
"The climate is constructive," Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti said after a two and a half hour meeting with Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) head Massimo D'Alema.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government does not include Refoundation but depends on the hard-left party for its majority in the lower house of parliament.

Bertinotti has met leading government figures in recent days to resolve deep differences between his party and the ruling coalition over a planned mini-budget, privatisations and a reform of the welfare state.
